steps.say: Coordinates give the position of a point. Read along the x-axis first, then up the y-axis.

figure.alt: A grid with point A at (4, 2).

steps.say: A helpful saying is along the corridor, then up the stairs.
To translate a point, slide it without turning. Moving 3 right and 2 up adds 3 to x and 2 to y.

figure.alt: Point A at (1, 2) and its translated image A' at (4, 4).

steps.say: A reflection flips a point over a mirror line. The image is the same distance from the line on the other side.
steps.show: P is 2 squares left of the line x = 4, so its image is 2 squares right

figure.alt: Point P at (2, 3) and its image P' at (6, 3), reflected in the line x = 4.

steps.say: When you reflect in a vertical mirror line, the y-coordinate stays the same.

check.prompt: What are the coordinates of point B?

figure.alt: A grid with point B, 3 along and 5 up.

hints: Then count up to the point.
check.explanation: B is 3 along and 5 up, so it is at (3, 5).

options.why: Count the squares along the x-axis again.
Read along the x-axis first, then up.

check.prompt: Point C is at (2, 6). It is translated 4 right and 3 down. Where is it now? Write it like (x, y).
hints: Moving right or left changes the x-coordinate.
Moving up or down changes the y-coordinate.

check.prompt: Point D is at (1, 4). It is reflected in the line x = 3. Where is its image?
hints: How far is D from the line x = 3?
The image is the same distance away on the other side.
D is 2 squares to the left of the line.
check.explanation: D is 2 squares left of x = 3, so the image is 2 squares right of it, at (5, 4).

options.why: That changes the y-coordinate. A vertical mirror line changes x.
That is on the mirror line. The image is on the other side.
D is 2 squares from the line, so the image is 2 squares past it.
